data.completion_memo: Implemented cross-platform native desktop presentation through Tauri on Windows, macOS, and Linux: native system/light/dark appearance projection, a complete application menu with workbench event routing, bounded native file and folder pickers, confirmation and informational OS message dialogs, OS notifications, show/hide/focus/minimize/maximize/fullscreen/close window actions, and a typed capability report. Native failures fall back to the existing accessible in-workbench status surface and focus-trapped confirmation dialog; browser/headless runs remain fully usable. Added a reproducible whole-application release assembler and executable build script. It builds and atomically publishes the desktop/core/worker/host/helper executables plus the complete UI closure, rejects symlinks/special files and existing outputs, normalizes permissions and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH timestamps, hashes every entry, emits protocol compatibility metadata and a design-compatible BuildProvenanceV1, and classifies packaged builds as package-owned with managed-local activation unavailable. The task-end audit ran the actual optimized release path: it produced all five binary roles plus the UI and verified provenance sha256:02b5cbd3ce7d90beb02d1f6ef6d907002c4c0583b8dd64dbdeeb8f6eee5766cc. Warnings-denied desktop Rust tests pass (20), frontend typecheck and 61 Vitest tests pass, bootstrap-helper tests pass (63), bash syntax and git diff checks are clean.
data.description: Implement Windows, macOS, and Linux bindings for platform appearance, application menus, file/folder and OS-message dialogs, notifications, window lifecycle, and accessible in-workbench fallback. Assemble reproducible whole-application bundles containing the core, worker, host, helper, and UI with protocol compatibility metadata and BuildProvenanceV1; packaged layouts must truthfully report managed-local self-activation Unsupported unless explicitly enrolled.
data.title: M12.4 — Implement native desktop presentation and whole-bundle release assembly
